messages.tray.title: Berill — system tray
messages.core.allSectionsInstalled: All sections are installed. New ones will appear here after an app update.
messages.core.autoSyncHint: On changes and on a schedule; otherwise only with the button
messages.core.deleteNoteText: The note will be removed from all your devices.
messages.core.e2eConfirmText: All records will be re-sent to the server encrypted. Other devices will pause syncing until you enter this password there. Write the password down: it can’t be recovered.
messages.core.e2eForget: Forget the key on this device
messages.core.e2eForgetText: Syncing will pause until you enter the password again.
messages.core.e2eLockedHint: Encryption was turned on on another device. Enter the same password to continue syncing.
messages.core.e2eOffHint: Right now the server stores your data in plain form. With encryption, field values are sent encrypted with a password only your devices know. The password can’t be recovered: if you forget it, the server copy can’t be read.
messages.core.e2eOnHint: On: values on the server are encrypted. The key is stored only on this device.
messages.core.e2eShort: At least 8 characters, both fields must match
messages.core.e2eSkipped: {n} encrypted records couldn’t be read — check the password
messages.core.noNotesYet: No notes yet. Tap “Note” to create your first one.
messages.core.noSectionsInstalled: No sections installed — add the ones you need from the catalog below.
messages.core.removeSectionText: The section will disappear from the sidebar and return to the catalog. Its entries aren’t deleted — reinstall it and everything will be back.
messages.core.sectionDisabledSettingsHint: This section is turned off or not installed — settings will be saved and applied once it’s turned on.
messages.core.sectionMissing: This section isn’t available in this version of the app.
messages.core.sectionUnavailable: This section is turned off or not installed. You can turn it on in Settings.
messages.core.sectionsHint: A turned-off section is hidden from the sidebar but stays installed. A removed one goes back to the catalog. Either way, its data is kept and keeps syncing.
messages.core.selectOrCreateNote: Select a note or create a new one
messages.core.syncAppearanceHint: Turn off to give this device its own look
messages.core.syncDataHint: While an item is off, its changes pile up on the device and go to the server once it’s turned back on. Data of removed sections keeps syncing as before — the item comes back with the section.
messages.core.syncFailed: Error: {message}. Your changes are saved and will be sent on the next attempt.
messages.core.syncNotConfigured: No server set up — data is stored on this device only.
messages.core.syncPluginSettingsHint: API keys, categories, goals and more
messages.core.syncSectionsHint: Which sections are installed and turned on
messages.external.installed: “{name}” is installed. Restart the app to enable it.
messages.external.notResponding: The plugin stopped responding — its process was stopped
messages.external.notSupported: Third-party plugins aren’t available on this device
messages.external.permissions: The plugin will get access to:
messages.external.removeText: The plugin will be removed after the app restarts. Its data stays.
messages.external.sectionHint: A third-party plugin runs in a separate isolated process: no access to files, other sections or the network except the sites it declares. Install plugins only from people you trust.
messages.external.tooManyCrashes: The plugin crashed repeatedly and was stopped: {reason}
messages.onboarding.accentText: The whole palette is built from it.
messages.onboarding.doneText: Your sections are in the sidebar. You can connect a sync server in Settings.
messages.onboarding.sectionsText: Turn on what you’ll use. The rest stays in the catalog — you can enable it later.
messages.onboarding.themeText: You can change the theme anytime in Settings.
messages.onboarding.welcomeText: Notes, habits, books, finances and everything else — in one place, on your phone and computer. Let’s set it up for you — it takes a minute.
messages.ui.accessDenied: access denied ({status}) — check the API key
messages.ui.deleteEverywhere: The entry will be removed on all devices.
messages.ui.networkNotAllowed: the section hasn’t declared access to {host}
messages.ui.tooManyRequests: too many requests, please wait a moment

messages.core.mcp.title: AI assistants (MCP)

messages.core.mcp.enableHint: Off. Assistants can't see your data

messages.core.mcp.desktopHint: JSON configuration for an MCP client supporting STDIO. The bridge starts Berill when needed.
messages.core.mcp.codeHint: For any compatible MCP client: server URL and Authorization header. Copy includes the token.
messages.core.mcp.tokenHint: Needed for HTTP connections. The --mcp bridge reads it by itself.
messages.core.mcp.regenerateText: Clients connected over HTTP with the old token lose access. Connections through --mcp keep working.
messages.connections.searchHint: Find something or run a command
messages.connections.clearTrashBody: All items in the trash will be permanently deleted.
messages.connections.deleteTrashBody: This item can no longer be restored.
messages.connections.dayEmpty: No events for this day yet
messages.connections.archiveHint: Local archive with notes, data and attachments
messages.connections.importConfirm: Archive data will be merged with your current records.
